key_insight: Current world models are judged too much by how well they generate convincing frames and not enough by whether they maintain a persistent internal state over time. The paper argues that a true world model must keep tracking objects and events even when they are not visible.
problem_solved: It addresses the evaluation gap in world-model benchmarks: existing tests often fail to check whether a model preserves a continuous, observer-independent representation of the world.
method: Identify persistent-state maintenance as a core requirement for world models, separate from image/video generation quality.
Critique current benchmarks for overlooking long-term object permanence and state evolution.
Frame evaluation around whether models can track hidden objects, ongoing events, and temporal continuity without direct observation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shifts attention from surface-level realism to deeper memory and state-tracking capabilities. It can guide the design of stronger benchmarks and more reliable embodied or planning-oriented agents.
visual_elements: A split diagram comparing frame generation vs persistent state tracking
A timeline showing objects continuing to evolve while unobserved
An icon-based benchmark checklist highlighting object permanence, hidden state, and event continuity
A simple pipeline graphic showing observation -> latent state -> future prediction
paper_title: Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core
paper_authors: Jinpeng Lu, Dexu Zhu, Haoyuan Shi, Linghan Cai, Guo Tang
